{{Quote|I'll let you come along on the next mission. Let's polish off a few more of those rough edges first. You can come next time, I promise.|Chankar Kim, to Enwandung-Esterhazy, before the Battle of Geonosis|<ref name="DR" />}}
'''Chankar Kim''' was a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] who lived during the last [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Sometime around [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Kim took [[Tallisibeth Enwandung-Esterhazy]] as her [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], even though the girl was weak in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. When fellow [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was captured during a mission on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], Kim was part of a [[Jedi assault team/Legends|Jedi strike team]] sent to rescue him. In the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|ensuing battle]], Kim was [[Death/Legends|killed]], leaving Enwandung-Esterhazy without a master.

==Biography==
{{Quote|I don't know what Chankar saw in her.''"<br />"''We'll never know now.|Mace Windu and Jai Maruk, on Kim and Enwandung-Esterhazy|<ref name="DR" />}}
[[File:Tallisibeth_Enwandung-Esterhazy.jpg|thumb|right|Tallisibeth Enwandung-Esterhazy, Chankar Kim's Padawan]]
Chankar Kim was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends]] during the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] before the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|outbreak]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="DR" /> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Death date" /> she took [[Tallisibeth Enwandung-Esterhazy]], nicknamed "Scout," as her [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], although even [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] member [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and other [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] failed to see what potential Kim saw in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]-weak girl.<ref name="DR" />

Three months after Kim took Scout as her Padawan,<ref name="DR" /> Jedi Knight [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was captured by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during a mission on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]]. Windu assembled a [[Jedi assault team/Legends|group of Jedi]] to free them,<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> and Kim was part of the task force. Before leaving, she told Scout that her Padawan would accompany her on the next mission. However, the rescue mission turned into a full-scale battle against the Confederate [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|droid army]], and Kim [[Death/Legends|fell]] in the fight<ref name="DR" /> in the [[Petranaki arena]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|217|Kim, Chankar}}</ref> leaving Scout an orphaned Padawan with a case of survivor's guilt.<ref name="DR" /> 

[[19 BBY/Legends|Three years later]], shortly before participating in a [[Jedi Temple Apprentice Tournament]] at the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Scout recalled the circumstances in which she had learned Kim would be her master and the circumstances of Kim's death. After Scout won the tournament, she received another Master, [[Jai Maruk]]. However, on their [[Mission to Vjun (Clone Wars)|first mission together]], Maruk was killed too, leaving Scout once again without a Master.<ref name="DR" />

==Personality and traits==
Chankar Kim took Scout as her Padawan, despite many Jedi failing to see potential in the seemingly ungifted girl.<ref name="DR" /> 

==Powers and abilities==
As a member of the Jedi Order, Kim was Force-sensitive and trained to [[Force power/Legends|wield]] the Force. She was capable enough to fight in the Battle of Geonosis, although despite being a Jedi Master, she became one of many Jedi killed in the fighting.<ref name="DR" />

==Behind the scenes==
Chankar Kim was first mentioned in ''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]'', a novel written by [[Sean Stewart]] and published in [[2004]].<ref name="DR" />
